body:
The twenty-seventh of September has fewer carpets than the day before. It has a grotto, a night list and a market.

I. After the refusal

The rejection still lies on the table. No one lays down new clauses. Araghchi still waits for the mediators to speak. Ship-counters say the blockade remains active. Thirteen passages the day before, one of them dark. Crude, earlier in the week, had been shoved through the needle in bursts, then thinned again.

Trump is in Tennessee. The offer to talk stands. So do the terms spoken on the lawn. Beijing repeats on Sunday that the two militaries should sign the memorandum on crisis channels. Washington slides another word into the machine file: Trump wants artificial intelligence called “superintelligence.” A Chinese foreign-ministry spokesman says Beijing respects the choice of term and will not adopt it.

Witkoff and Kushner sat three hours with mediators in the UN week. A second meeting had been called possible “in the very near future.” After the refusal on the lawn that sentence has no date. Tehran still says it will not surrender sovereign rights under pressure. Washington still says it already holds the water.

The tap stays where it was.

II. The night list from the east

In the morning Zelenskyy puts the week on the table. More than two thousand two hundred attack drones. About one thousand six hundred and fifty bombs from the air. Thirty-eight missiles, a share of them ballistic. Overnight into Sunday, three dead in Zaporizhzhia region. In Kyiv a man killed by a drone. Homes, power, roads in Odesa, Kharkiv, Sumy, Mykolaiv, Kherson, Poltava, Zhytomyr, Kyiv. In the morning a data centre in the capital is hit twice. Three wounded in the first blow, two of them children.

The field needs no metaphor. It has figures. Last week’s licence builds no battery today. In Sloviansk the damaged houses from Saturday still travel on Sunday wires. Putin remains invited to Miami. Brussels remains set to condemn the invasion there. Lavrov’s sentence from Saturday — see the war through to the end — needs no encore. It works alone.

Sunday changes no file in Miami. It changes the list of the dead.

III. The grotto

Leo XIV prays the Angelus in Lourdes. He asks that the rosary in October be said for peace. To the pilgrims: leave as missionaries of hope. To the French bishops: the Church still holds a prophetic voice in the public square; families are to be held. The sick are not to read their suffering as a sideline.

On the journey’s paper stands the meeting with survivors of clerical abuse. Seven of them, behind closed doors. Lourdes itself has carried, for years, a quarrel over art by an accused priest. The pope goes to the grotto anyway. Monday still holds Metz, Schuman’s city, and a sentence about Europe at war.

The Vatican sheet names the journey “That a world may have life.” Reconciliation as a programme. In Lourdes the programme meets crutches, water and files on offenders in the house. The pope remains in the country until Monday. A country that filled its square on Saturday sends the guest to the water under the rock. The thread is open. It does not end on Sunday.

IV. The market and the road

Saudi aircraft hit a market in Taiz. Seven dead, forty wounded. Riyadh speaks of Houthi positions. The city counts stalls. The war in Yemen keeps writing the same bill that reaches the pump by the Red Sea.

Near Munich a coach of tourists from the Philippines leaves the road. Two dead, twenty-five hurt. In Lwandle, Cape Town, ten people die in a shop; eleven are wounded. The police hunt the gunmen. Yesterday a tavern in Carletonville. Today a shop in Lwandle. The book counts taverns and shops because the great rooms do not.

V. At the edge of the page

British police clear houses near a base the Americans use in the south-west of England and detain men on suspicion of explosives. Ottawa counts which Canadian goods Washington will bar on Tuesday: alcohol, whey, molasses, motorcycles. In Madrid thousands walk over Ceuta. France elects its Senate by indirect vote. São Tomé and Príncipe elects an assembly. Switzerland votes.

The chronicler’s close

The refusal has grown no new clause overnight. The field has a week’s list. The guest has a grotto. The market in Taiz has seven names.

The World Book does not close. It leaves a finger in the pages and waits for 28 September.
